svg.text: THE SAME DOSE IS NOT THE SAME DOSE IN EVERY PATIENT
Age, pregnancy, liver and kidney change what the body does to the drug.

g.text: Kidneys clear more slowly — the
standard dose becomes an overdose
More sensitive to sedatives and to
anticholinergics — falls, confusion
Start low, go slow, review the list
Dose by weight, and weigh the child
today rather than using last month's
A child is not a small adult — the
liver and kidney are still maturing
Check the concentration on the bottle
Ask before prescribing, and ask again
before dispensing to a woman of
childbearing age
Untreated illness also harms the baby.
The answer is rarely simply to stop.
Kidney clears water-soluble drugs;
liver handles the rest
When either fails, the drug stays in
the body longer and accumulates
Reduce the dose or lengthen the gap
TYPE A — an exaggeration of the known effect. Predictable, dose-related, common. Reduce the dose.
TYPE B — unrelated to the known effect. Unpredictable, not dose-related, rare, often immune.
Stop the drug and record it as an allergy so nobody gives it again.

svg.text: Before any dose, ask three things: how old, is she pregnant, and how are the kidneys.
